_comment: Quality floors for fbtberger-raft. Both numbers may only go UP -- see the kwatro repository's QUALITY.md. Pitest is pointed at the arithmetic the protocol rests on (Quorum, RaftConfig, storage), not at RaftNode: one mutant there means booting a cluster.
_coverage_note: The floor is 0.85 against 85.47 % measured three times in a row on 2026-11-12 (374 tests, no failures). It is deliberately NOT the measured value. Ten lines in GrpcTransportServer's requestVote and appendEntries are recorded by JaCoCo in some runs and not in others with identical test outcomes, and ten of 2890 lines are 0.35 pp -- a floor at 85.47 % would redden a build that tested exactly as much as this one did. GrpcClusterTrafficTest asserts through a latch that both handlers were reached and is green in every run, including the runs where those lines read as uncovered. The code is exercised deterministically; the measurement is not. It happens with only those two tests selected, so it is not interference from the rest of the suite. Cause not established. 0.005 of slack in the ratchet is what keeps a floor set this way from nagging for an update on every run. History: the floor got to 0.84 in three steps on 2026-08-30 (84.8-85.3 % over three runs, 356 tests). The report stopped counting protoc output, which was two thirds of the lines and had nothing to do with the tests. The tests stopped sleeping: fixed waits became conditions, and where the code has an event to signal, latches on the RPC seam. And the three classes that were dark got tests -- RaftServer 0 to 53 %, RaftNodeConfiguration 38 to 79 %, RaftClient 39 to 70 %. What carried it from 0.84 to this reading is the eighteen tests since: the leader-lease read path, the TimeoutNow transfer fix, and the peer-RPC reentrancy fix, each arriving with its own.
